Data:Spintria.tin.json.Label: Tin Spintria
Data:Spintria.tin.json.Desc: Occult treasures are purchased with occult coin: spintriae. Tin spintriae usually display a wild face on their reverse side: shouting, screaming, or singing?

Data:Split.spintria.smithy.bronze.json.label: Divide Bronze
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.bronze.json.startdescription: Since the time of the Curia, the smiths of Brancrug have performed 'the service of division' for them. [This will break your spintria into more manageable coinage.]
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.bronze.json.desc: Denzil ushers me silently from the room while he does his work. I do not hear the sound of his hammer; perhaps he only keeps a secret cache of spintria. But when he comes out to hand me the coins, they are almost too hot to touch.

Data:Split.spintria.smithy.gold.json.label: Divide Gold
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.gold.json.startdescription: Since the time of the Curia, the smiths of Brancrug have performed 'the service of division' for them. [This will break your spintria into more manageable coinage.]
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.gold.json.desc: Denzil ushers me silently from the room while he does his work. I do not hear the sound of his hammer; perhaps he only keeps a secret cache of spintria. But when he comes out to hand me the coins, they are almost too hot to touch.

Data:Split.spintria.smithy.iron.json.label: 'Iron is Iron'
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.iron.json.startdescription: Since the time of the Curia, the smiths of Brancrug have performed 'the service of division' for the Librarian. But Denzil only shakes his head. 'Iron is iron,' is all he says.

Data:Split.spintria.smithy.silver.json.label: Divide Silver
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.silver.json.startdescription: Since the time of the Curia, the smiths of Brancrug have performed 'the service of division' for them. [This will break your spintria into more manageable coinage.]
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.silver.json.desc: Denzil ushers me silently from the room while he does his work. I do not hear the sound of his hammer; perhaps he only keeps a secret cache of spintria. But when he comes out to hand me the coins, they are almost too hot to touch.

Data:Split.spintria.smithy.tin.json.label: Divide Tin
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.tin.json.startdescription: Since the time of the Curia, the smiths of Brancrug have performed 'the service of division' for them. [This will break your spintria into more manageable coinage.]
Data:Split.spintria.smithy.tin.json.desc: Denzil ushers me silently from the room while he does his work. There is a brief sound - a kind of crackling shriek of joy or pain - that seems to come from within the smithy - but when I listen, it is not repeated. When Denzil comes out to hand me the coins, they are almost too hot to touch.

xexts.scrutiny: The architect's joy.

Data:Stag.finnian.json.Label: Finnian
Data:Stag.finnian.json.Desc: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals or adversaries whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

xexts.scrutiny: Finnian Boole was a tobacconist whose bills Westcott inexplicably refused to pay.

Data:Stag.hokobald.json.Label: Hokobald
Data:Stag.hokobald.json.Desc: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

xexts.scrutiny: The set of the mouth of the stag has, perhaps, a surly quality

Data:Stag.philemon.json.Label: Philemon
Data:Stag.philemon.json.Desc: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

xexts.scrutiny: Philemon was the nom de plume of a poet who satirically christened Westcott 'the Magus of the Silver'd Smoke'. Whatever this meant exactly, it clearly enraged Westcott.

Data:Stag.tavish.json.Label: Tavish
Data:Stag.tavish.json.Desc: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

xexts.scrutiny: Tavish is a gamekeeper who once derided Westcott's ability to shoot straight.

Data:Stand.umbrella.json.Label: Treasury of Shelters
Data:Stand.umbrella.json.Desc: It's like an armoury for not getting pneumonia.

xexts.scrutiny: A thick deposit has accrued to the bottom of the stand. A hundred years of rain applied to a hundred winters of mud.

Data:Stanislav.json.label: Fr. Stanislav John Schaller
Data:Stanislav.json.desc: Priest, diplomat, gardener: a soft-voiced man with a very steady gaze.

Data:Stargall.ink.json.Label: Stargall Ink
Data:Stargall.ink.json.Desc: An ink traditionally (but only rarely) made with meteoric iron; a minor Ink of Power.

xexts.scrutiny: Faintly glimmering. [There are Prentice-level Sky recipes which can create this.]

Data:Station.serving.gaol.json.label: Serve Here
Data:Station.serving.gaol.json.desc: Plates, cups and glasses, so that if I want to offer someone wine, I needn't give them the whole bottle.

Data:Station.serving.kitchen.json.label: Serve Here
Data:Station.serving.kitchen.json.desc: Plates, cups and glasses, so that if I want to offer someone wine, I needn't give them the whole bottle.

Data:Station.serving.lodge.json.label: Serve Here
Data:Station.serving.lodge.json.desc: Plates, cups and glasses, so that if I want to offer someone wine, I needn't give them the whole bottle.

Data:Statue.crozier.json.Label: 'Authority'
Data:Statue.crozier.json.Desc: Once this shepherd's crook represented the authority of the Church. Perhaps the Suppression Bureau kept it here because they liked the idea of authority, in general.

xexts.scrutiny: The Suppression Bureau, of course, is of a more ecclesiastical character than its progenitory Nocturnal Branch, though it has never had any official links to the Church Solar…

Data:Statue.debraose.json.Label: 'Lady de Braose'
Data:Statue.debraose.json.Desc: Sometimes known affectionately as 'the first Eva'. Lady de Braose never visited the Isle, but it was her generous endowment that allowed the Abbey to thrive and grow in the thirteenth century.

xexts.scrutiny: Why did Eva de Braose, the widow of a Marcher Lord from much further north, take such an interest in St Brandan's? There are stories…

Data:Statue.matilda.white.json.Label: White Matilda
Data:Statue.matilda.white.json.Desc: In 1093, twin infant girls were admitted to the care of the sisters here. Both were named Matilda. In 1127, the elder of the two became Abbess.

xexts.scrutiny: According to gossip and circumstantial evidence, the Matildas were illegitimate daughters of Gunnhild, daughter of King Harold, and a brother of the Earl of Cornwall - though which brother is a particularly murky question.

Data:Statue.rowena.json.Label: 'Lady Rowena'
Data:Statue.rowena.json.Desc: For as long as there has been a Hush House, there have been stories of its enigmatic protectress.

xexts.scrutiny: A Henry Moore piece - perhaps a genuine one. Moore did speak, very cautiously, of an 'encounter with a pale commission.'

Data:Statuette.bobo.nectar.json.Label: Bobos of Spring
Data:Statuette.bobo.nectar.json.Desc: A votive vessel for harvest offerings.

xexts.scrutiny: It might be construed as friendly.

Data:Statuette.cat.scale.json.Label: Cat of Depths
Data:Statuette.cat.scale.json.Desc: A votive offering to the Horned-Axe.

xexts.scrutiny: The Horned-Axe has been known to appreciate both owls and cats.

Data:Statuette.owl.moth.json.Label: Owl of Spirals
Data:Statuette.owl.moth.json.Desc: An ancient bird for an ancient place.

xexts.scrutiny: 'To every cry its beginning.'

Data:Statuette.pigeon.json.Label: Pigeon Statuette
Data:Statuette.pigeon.json.Desc: A beautifully enamelled little image. The maker's mark is 'AW'.

xexts.scrutiny: Was Ambrose Westcott really asked to provide a 'watcher of the skies?'

Data:Statuette.velvet.json.Label: 'The Velvet'
Data:Statuette.velvet.json.Desc: An Hour of secrecy? Ignorance? Privacy? Shame? The Velvet has never encouraged insight, investigation, or worship. Even an image of her is unusual.

xexts.scrutiny: The material is painted iron. The craftsmanship is commendable, but the artist's name has been obliterated by furious scratching and scoring.

Data:Status.rhonwen.open.json.label: Trust Active!
Data:Status.rhonwen.open.json.desc: Player has responded to Trust's initial letter.'

xexts.scrutiny: Appetite satisfied.

Data:Stone.indecipherable.json.Label: Inscribed Stone
Data:Stone.indecipherable.json.Desc: A stone tablet with rows of badly worn scratches that once, probably, were writing.

xexts.scrutiny: Successive Librarians all failed to decipher this tablet. It might as easily be a household inventory or an invocation to a god. Natalia Brulleau established a tradition that it always remain in the Librarian's quarters, to inspire her, and her successors, with humility and to illustrate the limits of knowledge.

Data:Stone.json.label: Stone
Data:Stone.json.desc: 'Ye who seek patience, here is your tutor.'

xexts.scrutiny: Someone has doggedly cleaned bird droppings and paint from this, not once but many times. The fabric is splotched and discoloured - the varnish of the wood is streaked like rain.
Someone has deliberately sanded down the end of each leg to a different angle.
The cushion is embroidered with the serpents of St Agnes.

Data:Stool.lavender.json.Label: Prison Stool
Data:Stool.lavender.json.Desc: A cheerful lavender colour, possibly to encourage rehabilitative enthusiasm.

xexts.scrutiny: Someone has scratched a series of tally marks down one leg. Seventy-seven days.
A stout little soldier, on whose worn surface have rested the slippers of a dozen generations of Librarians.

Data:Stool.moon.json.Label: Moon Stool
Data:Stool.moon.json.Desc: Polished to pallor by the posteriors of past Librarians.

xexts.scrutiny: A dark fruitwood - cherry? with very nicely executed joinery at the top.
Subtle, elegant fluting along each leg. Initialled L.T.P.

Data:Stool.plain.json.Label: Plain Stool
Data:Stool.plain.json.Desc: The most reliable object imaginable. How old is it?

xexts.scrutiny: It's older than one might expect. Very faintly, the triple knot can be made out on the underside of the seat…
